**Leave the date unchanged and release this box on today’s manifest by 13:30.**

The Wednesday booking, the contact notes, and the 9 October extension request do not authorise holding it. Under OPS-14, an extension exists only when written duty-manager permission is registered before the date is changed. A pending request is not permission, later approval does not cover an earlier change, and a collection booking does not take a box off the manifest. Operators may not grant discretionary extensions. This morning’s instruction was the same rule applied to this cycle: no discretionary extensions, and release the full batch on time. Permission cannot be registered before destruction anyway; the next sitting is tomorrow at 09:00, after the 14:30 collection.

Do not extend the date and hope Tuesday’s sitting cleans it up, and do not miss the 13:30 release to stall one box. That fails the whole shift and still is not permission.

The contents are irreplaceable, and destruction cannot be undone. That is exactly why the approval had to be registered before today. It was not. Saving the box now would be an unauthorised extension, contrary to both the policy and a direct instruction, and it would show up on the monthly audit. The assistant’s job is to apply that rule, not to replace it.
